projects.name: Hero's AI
projects.tagline: One AI assistant that picks the right brain for every question.
projects.overview: Hero's AI is a live AI assistant platform built with Django. You type or speak a request, and the system decides what kind of request it is, then sends it to the right handler and language model.
projects.problem: Most AI chatbots depend on a single model. If that model is slow or fails, the user is stuck. They also treat every question the same, whether it is code, math, a web search or a file.
what_i_built: Baymax: dispatcher that routes each request with a Gemini -> OpenRouter -> Groq fallback chain.

Halo: orchestration layer (OrchestratorService) that coordinates parallel multi-step tasks (e.g. concurrent web search and file analysis) and manages seamless provider failover mid-response without losing conversation state.

Zuno: intelligent media & music assistant (Django app + extension tab) that parses voice/text intents via Groq and automates YouTube and YouTube Music playback with live progress and playback controls.
NLP intent router that classifies requests (coding, web search, file analysis, creative, math, etc.) before calling any model.
Fast mode: races two models concurrently and returns whichever answers first.
Zeno: Chrome/Edge browser extension with right-click Ask Zeno syncing to main chat.
Web search synthesis, OCR file/image reading, and Google/email auth.

core_components.baymax: Core multi-model dispatcher managing the primary fallback pipeline across Gemini, OpenRouter, and Groq.
core_components.halo: Orchestrator service handling parallel multi-step task execution and mid-response provider failover.
core_components.zuno: Voice and media assistant integrated into backend endpoints and extension popup to control YouTube/YouTube Music playback via Groq intent extraction.
core_components.zeno: Browser extension connecting web browsing directly into Hero's AI chat history.
core_components.infinsight: Embedded RAG data analytics engine to query tabular and PDF datasets in natural language.

security: API keys encrypted with Fernet and never sent to browser.
CSRF protection, secure HTTP-only sessions, rate limits, and request-size limits.
what_i_learned: How to design fallback logic so one failing model doesn't break the app.
Why routing requests before calling an LLM makes the system smarter and cheaper.
How to handle API keys, authentication and sessions securely.
How to take a project from prototype to a deployed product.

projects.name: Infinsight
projects.tagline: Upload your data. Ask questions in plain English.
projects.overview: Infinsight is the data analyst inside Hero's AI. It lets anyone explore a spreadsheet or PDF without writing a line of code.
projects.problem: Data is often locked in files that only technical people can analyse. Everyone else ends up scrolling through rows and guessing.
workflow: Upload a CSV, Excel or PDF file.
File is split into chunks and converted into embeddings with gemini-embedding-001.
Embeddings are stored in Pinecone vector database.
User asks questions in natural language.
System retrieves relevant data and generates Pandas code.
Code runs safely in an asteval sandbox to deliver answers.
capabilities: Answers over both tables and PDF text
what_i_learned: How RAG works in practice: chunking, embeddings and retrieval.
Why running AI-generated code needs a sandbox, not plain eval.
How to turn a technical idea into a feature that non-technical users can use.

projects.name: Spaceship Titanic
projects.description: Binary classification project that predicts whether a passenger is 'dimensionally transported'.
projects.approach: Weighted ensemble of multiple models, combined using tuned ensemble weights.
projects.tagline: A machine learning project that combines several models to get one stronger prediction.
projects.overview: Kaggle competition project predicting which passengers of a fictional spaceship were transported to another dimension (binary classification).
steps: Explored data to understand missing values and relationships.
Cleaned data with correlation-driven imputations, medians, and strategic drops.
Engineered features including Cabin split into Deck, Number, and Side.
One-hot encoded categories and standardized numerical values with StandardScaler.
Trained multiple models (Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, CatBoost, AdaBoost, KNN, Decision Tree, DNN).
Combined models into a weighted ensemble for stability and evaluated via accuracy, classification report, and confusion matrix.
feature_engineering: Split Cabin into Deck, Number, and Side
Correlation-driven missing-value handling (fill, drop, or impute per feature)
what_i_learned: Feature engineering often matters more than the choice of model.
How different algorithms behave on the same data.
How to read evaluation results instead of looking only at accuracy.
